title: Metric evolution policy and trace retention lifecycle
content:
Purpose
---
This doc proposes a compact policy for how metrics evolve, how traces are retained/archived, and concrete dashboard layout guidance to keep investigation latency low while bounding telemetry cost. Focus is on inference-serving signals (token latency, kv-cache warmth, model-fanout, routing fallbacks) but the policy is generalizable.

High-level goals
- Keep hot investigation signal available with full fidelity for 7 days.
- Provide aggregated/derived signal slices for 30/90/365 day windows for trending and alerting.
- Limit cardinality explosion from dynamic labels (tenant/request tags) via a tiered sampling + index strategy.
- Define metric evolution process (rename, deprecate, migrate) to avoid dashboard rot.
- Ensure trace artifacts required for root-cause are retrievable within SLA and cost budgets.

Key concepts and definitions
- Raw trace: full span sequence + attributes for a single request.
- Compact trace: sampled trace with redacted/high-level attributes (no full prompt payloads).
- Metric canonical: stable metric name + owner + semantic description (used in dashboards and SLIs).
- Metric variant: temporary metric names used for experiments (tagged with migration ticket).
- Signal lane: retention profile (hot/warm/archived) applied consistently across metrics/traces.

Retention lanes (proposal)
- Hot lane (7 days, full fidelity): raw traces, high-cardinality metrics (unaggregated), span logs. Purpose: immediate RCA, incident window.
- Warm lane (30 days, reduced fidelity): compact traces (redacted), aggregated high-cardinality metrics at tenant-quantiles, retention of metric rollups at 1-minute granularity.
- Cold lane (90 days, summaries): daily rollups, percentile history, SLI time series at 5m granularity.
- Archive lane (365+ days): compressed indexes (no traces), monthly rollups for long-term trends and compliance export.

Sampling policy (trace-level)
- Baseline: 0.5% of all requests kept as raw traces globally.
- Error-bound sampling: 100% raw traces for requests that triggered errors, model fallback, or high token hallucination score (automated flag).
- Tenant-weighted boost: tenants with active oncall or escalations get a higher sampling floor (1–5%). Controlled via oncall tag.
- Burst capture: if an SLI breach is detected for a route, temporarily increase sampling to 5–10% for a 1h window for that route.
- Adaptive reservoir: maintain per-route reservoir to ensure low-traffic critical routes still capture traces.

Trace anonymization rules
- Never retain full prompt text in cold/archive lanes. Strip or hash any PII.
- For hot lane, prompt text kept but access limited via RBAC and audit logs.
- All traces stored in archive must be transformed to remove embeddings and full prompt bodies. Only metadata and hashes allowed.

Metric evolution lifecycle
1) Proposal stage: engineer files a migration ticket (JIRA) and creates a metric-canonical proposal in telemetry board. Include rationales, owners, existing dashboards using metric.
2) Dual-write window (30 days suggested): new metric emitted alongside old, dashboards gradually switched, alerts mirrored to ensure parity.
3) Deprecation announcement: after parity confirmed, schedule deprecation; update docs; set sunset date.
4) Removal: after sunset and stakeholder sign-off, metric removed from instrumentation and archived.
5) Audit: monthly review of deprecated metrics older than 90 days for hard delete.

Dashboard design guidance (investigation-first)
- Panels should be grouped by investigative goal, not by raw metric namespace. Example groups: Latency Attribution, Cache Warmth & Eviction, Model Routing & Fallbacks, Error Modes.
- Keep a 2x2 microtile layout per group: overview quantiles (P50/P90/P99), heatmap (latency slices by token-position), event-rate, top correlated tags (tenant/route/model).
- Correlation anchors: every latency panel must link to a trace-sampling quicklink and a prompt-replay entry (if available).
- Default time windows: 30m / 6h / 7d presets in top-right. Operators need a "zoom-to-incident" button that jumps dashboard to alert window.
- Cost-aware widgets: avoid uncontrolled list widgets that explode cardinality — require an explicit filter before expanding to top-N.

Cardinality controls
- Forbidden labels by default on high-cardinality metrics: request_id, user_prompt_hash, full_session_id. Use hashed_binned_session_id if needed.
- Tag-whitelist: teams must register nonstandard tags in telemetry catalog. Unregistered dynamic tags will be auto-sampled at ingestion.
- Top-N enforcement: dashboards showing tag-distribution must default to top-10 and offer explicit expand action.

SLI mapping examples
- Token TTF (time to first token) -> objective: 99th percentile < 250ms for hosted tier; primary metric: ttf_p99_route.
- Cold-cache latency -> objective: 95th percentile < 600ms; signal: cold_kv_latency_p95, probe: synthetic cold-start probe.
- Model-fallback rate -> objective: <= 0.2% per hour; signal: fallback_rate_per_1m.

Investigation play snippets (how to use these signals)
1) Start with SLI spike panel (30m). If spike present, open correlated rate and model-fallback panel.
2) Jump to trace sampling quicklink for that route/time window and check any raw traces emitted.
3) If no raw traces, inspect warm lane compact traces and tenant-weighted histograms.
4) Validate KV-cache warmth by checking prefix-warmth metric and recent eviction spikes.
5) If model-specific, pull model-sidecar logs via trace id and open the performance annotation.

Cost budget and telemetry quotas (initial guardrails)
- Reserve telemetry cost to 3% of infra budget for production observability.
- Trace budget: cap raw trace store to X GB/day (placeholder to be set by finance). Enforce ingestion throttles when approaching cap.
- Aggregation policy: fallback to 1m rollups when daily ingestion > threshold.

Open questions / TODOs
- Define concrete GB/day trace budget and quota enforcement thresholds (Finance + Eng infra).
- Decide whether to store hashed prompt snippets for 30 days (privacy/legal consult).
- Finalize tooling for dual-write detection and dashboard migration automation (PR in telemetry repo).
- Create small-run experiment to validate reservoir sampling for low-traffic but critical tenant routes.

Quick action items (short-term)
- [ ] Create JIRA template for metric evolution (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Pilot adaptive sampling on one high-throughput route for 2 weeks (owner: Liam).
- [ ] Implement RBAC gate on prompt text retrieval in hot lane (owner: Diego).
- [ ] Draft finance-backed trace budget and enforcement knobs (owner: Maya).

Notes to self / workshop fragments
- Sketch: dashboard microtile that shows latency waterfall colored by model step (tokenization, attention, kv-lookup, decode).
- Workshop idea: 90-minute "metric surgery" where product + ops bring top 20 panels and we map ownership -> canonical names -> migration path.
- Keep a "lightweight" timeline for deprecations so PMs can plan customer-facing changes.

- Telemetry PR for reservoir sampling: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/88
